source.title: Is deeper better? It depends on locality of relevant features

page_placements.theme: Architecture and inductive bias govern benefits of capacity

record.tranche_reason: The paper measures test error while varying network width and training-set size, but it does not reproduce a double-descent sweep around the interpolation threshold.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test-error results for width and training-sample sweeps. These bear on the model-size and sample-size versions, but the text does not identify an interpolation threshold or report a complete double-descent curve. NTK comparisons are included only where they contribute to the reported test-error comparisons; cited double-descent results are not recorded as this study’s findings.
record.test_reason: The study asks how depth affects generalization, and every network it trains is overparameterized. No model size, epoch count or sample size is swept through an interpolation threshold, so no fall-rise-fall curve or near-threshold sample effect can show up. Double descent appears only as background in the introduction (refs 10, 11, 14). Its width trends (wider is better among 2–4 overparameterized widths) say nothing about whether a peak exists. They are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The authors conclude that deeper is better for local labels and shallower is better for global labels. They propose chaotic signal propagation as the mechanism, and argue that the NTK misses the depth dependence, so feature learning matters. They draw no conclusion about double descent.
record.recipe_differences: Synthetic Gaussian-input classification with local and global labels; fully connected networks are compared across selected widths, depths, and training-set sizes rather than conducting a double-descent sweep through the interpolation threshold.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported generalization results vary with label locality, depth, width, loss function, and learning rate. The paper also reports differences between finite networks and the NTK.

fits_no_version.finding: In the overparameterized regime, increasing width lowers both test error and run-to-run variance. Examples: 1-local and 1-global labels (Fig. 1), 3-local at L=7 (Fig. 2b), and 3-global at L=7 (Fig. 2d).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Beyond the interpolation regime, wider fully connected nets generalize better and with lower initialization variance, at fixed depth.

fits_no_version.finding: Raw parameter count does not predict generalization across depths. On k-local labels, L=7, H=100 (~1e5 parameters) beats L=1, H=2000 (~1e6 parameters). Test error falls with depth for 2-local labels and rises with depth for 2-global labels (Fig. 3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Generalization in overparameterized nets depends on architecture (depth relative to feature locality), not only on parameter count.

record.problems: The width comparisons use selected architectures and do not span an identified interpolation threshold. Several plotted outcomes are not numerically tabulated; training variability is reported for 10 iterations. The tasks are primarily artificial.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for each plotted architecture and training-set-size point; the text does not provide those point values, and the figures show multiple architecture curves. The reported text-level width and sample-size findings are represented in r1-r3 and r5-r6. The Ising-model test-error curves in Supplementary Fig. S2 vary sample size but do not report a threshold or a textual finding that more data raises error.

untested.parts: All of it. No width sweep through the interpolation threshold; only 2–4 overparameterized widths are compared.
All of it. Training stops once training error is zero, and no test-error-vs-epoch curve is reported.
All of it. The sample-size sweeps stay far from the threshold.
All of it. Only fully connected networks and the NTK are used, with no capacity sweep past interpolation.
All of it. No effective-complexity measure is proposed.
All of it. There is no label noise, no peak, and no regularization sweep; the learning-rate dependence in Fig. 4 is not a regularization test of a peak.
All of it. Complexity is never re-expressed as an effective parameter count.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' relation and the V1 limits_scope label are overturned. Absence of a peak in a study that never approaches the threshold is not evidence about any version. The Ising results (Supp. Fig. S2) and the mean-square-loss results (Fig. S1) also stay in the overparameterized regime and are likewise irrelevant to V1–V7.

versions.untested_parts: The paper compares selected widths in an overparameterized setting but does not sweep model size through the interpolation threshold or report the full fall-rise-fall curve.
Test error over training epochs is not reported as a curve; training stops when training error reaches zero.
Training-set size is varied, but the paper does not locate the interpolation threshold or specifically test whether adding samples near it raises test error.
No general double-descent curve across model classes is tested.
No single effective-complexity measure is proposed or tested across axes.
The paper does not test noise-driven peaks, multiple descent peaks, or optimally tuned regularization.
The paper does not re-express model complexity as an effective parameter count or test whether that removes the second descent.

rows.subject: Fully connected ReLU networks, 1-local and 1-global label experiments
rows.size_stated: Widths 100, 500, 2000, as plotted; depths 1 and 7, plus a depth-0 linear perceptron
rows.operation_detail: Compared test error across selected network widths.
rows.value: The text states that test error decreases with network width; exact values are figure only.
rows.note: The text also reports that shallower networks outperform deeper ones and that the linear perceptron performs best. The plotted widths are selected architectures, not a continuous sweep through an interpolation threshold.
rows.check: Only 2–3 widths are compared, all overparameterized and trained to zero training error. 'Test error decreases with width' covers only the region past the threshold and cannot show V1's peak or curve. Width is also confounded with depth (L=1 vs 7) and a linear perceptron.

rows.subject: Fully connected ReLU networks, k-local label experiments
rows.operation_detail: Compared test error across selected widths and depths.
rows.value: The text states that increasing width decreases test error and variance; exact values are figure only.
rows.uncertainty: Standard deviation over 10 initialization and training iterations; the text notes large error bars for depth 7, width 100 on the 3-local task.
rows.note: The reported width trend is in selected settings. The depth-7, width-100 network fails on the 3-local task for small training sets.
rows.check: Same issue: selected overparameterized widths only, with no interpolation threshold crossed. The width/variance finding is linked by the authors to lazy-regime variance work, not tested as double descent.

rows.subject: Fully connected ReLU networks, k-global label experiments
rows.operation_detail: Compared test error across selected widths and depths.
rows.value: The text states that shallow networks outperform deep ones; for depth 7, wider networks improve more quickly with training-set size. Exact values are figure only.
rows.uncertainty: Standard deviation over 10 initialization and training iterations.
rows.note: This result concerns selected widths and depths and does not establish a model-size double-descent curve.
rows.check: This is a depth comparison plus a width effect at L=7 within the overparameterized regime. It does not bear on the model-wise double-descent shape.

rows.subject: Fully connected ReLU networks, 2-local and 2-global label experiments
rows.operation_detail: Compared test error across network depths at fixed width.
rows.value: Test error decreases with depth for the 2-local label and increases with depth for the 2-global label; exact values are figure only.
rows.uncertainty: Standard deviation over 10 training iterations using the same dataset.
rows.note: Depth is varied, not model size; this result does not itself test V1’s model-size curve.
rows.check: A depth sweep (L=1–10) at fixed width and N, all overparameterized. It is not the model-size axis of V1 and spans no threshold.

rows.operation_detail: Varied the number of training samples and measured test error.
rows.measure: Test error as a function of training-set size
rows.value: Figure only; the text describes minor improvement with sample size for the depth-7, width-100 3-global network and improvement for wider networks, but does not state that adding data raises test error.

rows.note: The sample-size curves do not identify an interpolation threshold or establish behavior near it.
rows.check: Same as r5: the sample-size sweep stays deep in the overparameterized regime. The text reports only stagnant or improving error with N (e.g. minor improvement for L=7, H=100 on 3-global), never a rise.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

rows.locator_found: Sec. 3.2, paragraph immediately preceding Sec. 3.3; Fig. 3 and caption.

relation.reason: Double descent appears as cited background in the introduction; the study's own results concern locality, depth, width, and feature learning.

tranche.reason: The experiments compare generalization within an overparameterized regime without testing an interpolation peak, epoch-wise double descent, near-threshold sample effects, or another claim version.

source_check.notes: The authors-conclusion paraphrase is supported. The r4 depth trend is explicitly stated in Sec. 3.2, although its locator is marked figure_only.

statements.correction: For d=500, L=7, H=100 has approximately 1e5 parameters; L=1, H=2000 has approximately 1e6. The former outperforms the latter for 2-local labels and for 3-local labels at large N; it fails on 3-local labels at small N. At H=500 and N=10000, increasing depth decreases 2-local test error and increases 2-global test error.
statements.problem: The parameter counts and depth trends are supported, but the k-local comparison omits qualifications: the 3-local advantage requires large N, and the parameter counts are stated for d=500.
